NVDA.headline: AI bubble debate and rival chip push weigh on shares
NVDA.summary: Investors are divided over whether recent AI bubble warnings are significant, with concern centred on heavy infrastructure spending and debt-funded firms such as CoreWeave. Microsoft's Maia 300 accelerator plans have also drawn attention, though analysts say Maia is a small share of Microsoft's AI chip spend. Shares fell 1.43% today and are down 2.38% over one month.

MSFT.headline: Microsoft disrupts phishing kits; faces lawsuits and game report
MSFT.summary: Microsoft and Health-ISAC seized domains used by three Chinese-language phishing services linked to over 1bn malicious messages. Eight US states have sued OpenAI, and a report claims Microsoft cancelled an unannounced Fallout game, without official comment. Meta reported a GitHub intrusion affecting about 1,500 people, though it is not a Microsoft matter. Shares fell 1.93% today.

AAPL.headline: iPhone Duo demand strong, but shipping dates slip into 2027
AAPL.summary: Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, started preorders at $1,999, with Apple calling demand extraordinary, though US shipping estimates have moved as late as January 2027. Apple's CEO called memory chip shortages a crisis, and the company is partnering with Meta to run an open model on Mac Studio. Shares rose 0.43% today and are up 36.14% over one year.

GOOGL.headline: News AI pilot expands; Sergey Brin on self-improving AI
GOOGL.summary: Google's News AI pilot now includes more than 400 publications, including CNN and the Financial Times, and Google has changed how links appear in AI search answers. Sergey Brin said Gemini is now helping build the next Gemini, and a UK proposal to extend the BBC licence fee to streamers was reported but not confirmed. Shares fell 2.47% today, with no company-specific cause given in the stories.

AMZN.headline: Bee wearables launch; reports of AI chip sale and acquisition
AMZN.summary: Amazon launched two Bee AI wearables, priced at $74.99 and $99.99, with the second due shortly. Unconfirmed reports say Amazon may sell around $8bn of Nvidia chips to investors and is pursuing another AI acquisition, and it is reportedly planning AI and robotics for delivery stations. Amazon is also reported to be restricting AI agents on its site. Shares fell 1.87% today.

META.headline: Ofcom fine challenge and scraping terms change; shares drop
META.summary: Meta is challenging how Ofcom calculates online safety fines in the High Court, and has removed language that could have allowed scraping of news sites for AI training, saying content owners can still use robots.txt. A reported GitHub breach affected about 1,500 people. Investors are looking to Meta's upcoming earnings for AI spending clarity. Shares fell 3.72% today.

AVGO.headline: Microsoft's Maia push and sector selloff weigh on shares
AVGO.summary: Broadcom shares fell 4.52% today to 328.75 USD, and are down 5.34% over one month. Microsoft's plans to make its in-house Maia 300 accelerator its main inference system, and a report of the chip index's longest losing streak since 2008, form the backdrop. Broadcom is also named among large US companies objecting to a proposed framework for tokenised stocks.

TSLA.headline: Roadster reveal draws mixed reaction; Musk comments on AI and debt
TSLA.summary: Tesla shares fell 2.13% today to 354.72 USD, and are down 3.13% over one month. Coverage of the second-generation Roadster, with production now planned for 2028 and $50,000 or $250,000 reservations, is largely sceptical, and the FAA says it is not an aircraft. A separate report says Elon Musk told Walter Isaacson that AI and robotics are the only realistic fix for US debt, and Bloomberg reports EV-era factories shifting to grid batteries. One unverified feed item claims a flying car, which should be treated with caution.

TSM.headline: Record profit, but TSMC cautious on 2027 amid AI selloff
TSM.summary: TSMC reported a record third-quarter net profit of NT$763.1bn, up 69% year on year, and forecast about 44% dollar revenue growth for 2026. Chairman C.C. Wei warned of pressure in consumer markets and said TSMC is being prudent about 2027. Chip stocks have sold off sharply, and Taiwan and China are tightening rules on AI chip exports. Shares fell 2.28% today.

BRK-B.headline: Berkshire adds $330m to Bending Spoons stake
BRK-B.summary: Berkshire Hathaway B shares rose 1.21% today to 532.02 USD, and are up 4.48% over one month. The company has agreed to buy 10 million new Bending Spoons shares at $33 each in a $330m private placement, adding to its $600m investment at the Nasdaq listing in July. The deal still needs closing conditions and an SEC filing. Mizuho described it as a vote of confidence in the company's model.

LLY.headline: No major news; shares edge higher
LLY.summary: There is no major news right now. Eli Lilly shares rose 0.43% today to 1,257.03 USD, are up 9.08% over one month and 56.57% over one year, and trade near the top of their 52-week range.

JPM.headline: Bill yields rise and UK bank tax reports weigh on outlook
JPM.summary: JPMorgan Chase shares rose 1.25% today to 339.72 USD, though they are down 2.75% over one month. Bloomberg reports a record-low-demand eight-week bill auction cleared at 4.05%, while overnight repo markets remain calm. Separately, UK reports say a bank tax rise may be included in the Budget, and UBS has warned it could raise mortgage costs. A MarketWatch piece says the Fed's coming decision is a closer call than markets think.

WMT.headline: Universal Cart rollout and consumer spending commentary
WMT.summary: Walmart shares rose 0.8% today to 118.81 USD, and are up 11.26% over one month and 10.28% over one year. Google has begun rolling out Universal Cart in the US, which supports in-interface purchases from Walmart, and a Wells Fargo economist said US consumers are battered but still spending. Several sites, including Amazon, are restricting AI shopping agents, which could limit agent-driven shopping.

V.headline: No major news right now
V.summary: There is no major news right now for Visa. The shares are up 0.72% today and 8.83% over one month, and up 17.76% over one year. The stock trades at $402.61, near the top of its 52-week range of $293.89 to $404.74.

XOM.headline: Higher refining margins could add $4.5B to Q3 earnings
XOM.summary: ExxonMobil told investors in an 8-K filing that higher third-quarter refining margins could lift downstream profit by about $4.5 billion, on top of $4.1 billion from refining in the second quarter. Brent crude reached $110 a barrel for the first time since May, and the shares rose 2.46% today and 59.46% over the past year, near the top of their 52-week range. Reports also cite a US move to soften its stance on Russian oil sanctions, though the specific measures are unclear.

JNJ.headline: No major news right now
JNJ.summary: There is no major news right now for Johnson & Johnson. The shares rose 0.9% today but are down 5.43% over the past month, while still up 32.26% over the past year.

SPCX.headline: Space sector interest grows; no major company-specific news
SPCX.summary: Reports cover the US Army expanding space forces, a Chinese-linked group taking a roughly $434m stake in Canada's MDA Space, and Rocket Lab delaying Neutron to 2027. None of the stories is specific to Space Exploration Technologies. Shares fell 1.74% today and are down 5.67% over one month.

MU.headline: Memory shortage warnings from Apple and Dell
MU.summary: Micron shares fell 5.63% today to 878.84 USD, and are down 10.09% over one month, though up 334.25% over one year. Apple's John Ternus called memory chip supply constraints a crisis, and Michael Dell said shortages of HBM and DRAM could worsen in 2027. Reports say SK hynix's US subsidiary Solidigm has hired lobbyists over China-related restrictions, but none of these plans has been confirmed by the companies.

AMD.headline: Chip sector selloff and Nvidia GeForce supply reports
AMD.summary: AMD shares fell 5.95% today to 528.75 USD, and are down 3% over one month but up 126.85% over one year. The chip index SOX has reportedly posted its longest losing streak since 2008 amid AI worries. Intel's Nova Lake and Razor Lake-AX timelines were also reported, with Nova Lake due in 2027 and Razor Lake-AX in 2028.

ASML.headline: Chip sector demand strong as TSMC reports record profit
ASML.summary: ASML shares were down 0.38% today at 1641.52 USD, up 0.73% over one month and 59.48% over one year. The move follows TSMC's record third-quarter profit, which rose 69% year on year, with 2026 dollar revenue growth guided at about 44%. TSMC chairman C.C. Wei was more cautious on 2027 and flagged pressure in consumer and price-sensitive markets, while saying AI-driven chip demand still far exceeds supply.

SMT.L.headline: Shares fall 3.1% amid Scottish politics and Diageo spill news
SMT.L.summary: Scottish Mortgage shares fell 3.13% today to 1545 GBp, though they remain up 4.53% over one month and 39.57% over one year. Coverage this period centres on Scottish independence and devolution debates between the SNP and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, which the reports describe as political rather than market-moving. A Diageo caustic soda spill in a River Spey tributary is also reported, but the feed gives no link to the trust's holdings or share price.

ARQQ.headline: No major news; shares down 11.82% today
ARQQ.summary: There is no major news right now for Arqit Quantum Inc. The shares are priced at 14.02 USD, down 11.82% today and 28.18% over the past month. Over the past year they are down 66.21%, trading near the lower end of their 52-week range of 11.52–49.33 USD.

RGTI.headline: No major news; shares down 6.57% today
RGTI.summary: There is no major news right now for Rigetti Computing, Inc. The shares are priced at 11.80 USD, down 6.57% today and 26.2% over the past month. Over the past year they are down 74.56%, trading near the lower end of their 52-week range of 11.11–47.78 USD.
